title: Profit is not the same as cash
deck: Connect earnings, cash movement, and the balance sheet with a small worked example.
authors: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission · Office of Investor Education and Advocacy
takeaways: Profit and cash generation answer different questions.
Footnotes explain choices behind the reported numbers.

sections.heading: A snapshot and two flows
paragraphs: A balance sheet records assets, obligations, and owners’ interest at one date. Income measures earnings over a period; cash flow tracks cash movements.
The fourth statement tracks changes in owners’ equity.

sections.heading: Cash has three routes
paragraphs: The guide separates operating cash from investment purchases or sales and financing such as borrowing, repayments, and share issuance.

sections.heading: Read beyond the headline
paragraphs: Footnotes explain accounting policies and other details. Management’s discussion supplies context, trends, and risks. Useful ratios depend on the industry.

sections.heading: Original example · a hypothetical business
paragraphs: This researchx example is authored for learning; it is not from the SEC guide. Begin with $50 cash funded entirely by the owner. Earn $100 revenue, collect $80, and incur $60 expenses paid in cash. There are no other transactions.

Profit is $40, but operating cash flow is $20. Cash closes at $70, and customers still owe $20. Closing assets of $90 equal equity of $90: the initial $50 plus $40 retained profit. This is an educational illustration, not an investment recommendation.

quote.text: No one financial statement tells the complete story.
quote.locator: Bringing It All Together, final paragraph

caveats.heading: Introductory scope
caveats.text: This 2007 guide introduces financial statements; it does not provide company-specific analysis.

caveats.heading: A simplified model
caveats.text: The original example assumes no debt, taxes, investing, financing, depreciation, dividends, or other opening assets and liabilities.

references.label: How cash connects to earnings

interaction.title: Follow one sale through the statements
interaction.description: Adjust cash collected from $10 to $100 against a fictional business’s $100 revenue. Keep expenses at $60, paid in cash, and opening cash at $50. Compare profit, operating cash, receivables, and the linked balance sheet.
interaction.boundary: Original researchx educational model. No debt, taxes, other flows, or opening receivables. The business retains its profit. This is not an investment recommendation.
